decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is only now being released, with a Q1/2019 date, so its results cannot yet be judged against aspirations, and the firm's specialised dosimetry slack lets it carry the product through rollout.
Small volume ionization chambers are core dosimetry consumables that fit the firm's calibration business, so no shortfall is evident that would prompt a search for other uses of the resources.
A second small volume chamber may overlap with Product B, but it costs little to carry inside an established catalogue, and nothing signals that it falls short of aspirations.
The standard clinical chamber line with several models is a staple of the reference dosimetry business and likely meets its aspirations.
The relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantom systems and sells into a steady demand, so management has no reason to begin a search for alternatives.
Thimble chambers are established dosimetry products with stable demand, so this one is likely judged satisfactory and kept.
